title: Value of the ±1 embedding at a true coordinate
statement: Let $x$ be a binary word of length $n$, and let $s(x) \in \bbr^n$ denote its $\pm1$ embedding, whose $i$-th coordinate is $-1$ when $x_i$ is true and $+1$ when $x_i$ is false. Then for every index $i$ with $x_i$ true, the $i$-th coordinate of $s(x)$ equals $-1$.
hypotheses_covered: x is a binary word of length n
i is an index with x_i = true
replaced:
Let $x$ be a binary word of length $n$, that is, a function assigning to each index $i
\in \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ a boolean value, and let $\mathrm{pmOne}(x) \in \bbr^n$ be the
real vector whose $i$-th coordinate equals $-1$ when $x_i$ is true and $+1$ when $x_i$
is false. Then for any index $i$ at which $x_i$ is true, the $i$-th coordinate of
$\mathrm{pmOne}(x)$ equals $-1$.
